payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does comparison with the input image show that adding a helmet to the woman is an edit made in response to the request?
node.criteria: Pass if comparison shows the helmet was added to the woman; fail if comparison clearly shows no requested change was made; unknown if the comparison cannot establish whether the helmet was added.
node.binding: The requested change is adding a helmet to the woman, not an unrelated edit.

node_traces.evidence: Comparing the images, the edited image shows a helmet on the woman's head that is absent in the source image.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image clearly shows the woman wearing a helmet on her head.

fulfillment: The node is already performing well: the edited image visibly adds a helmet on the woman’s head, and both endpoint and source-comparison traces support completion with high confidence. No semantic change is indicated by this evaluation. For robustness, preserve the distinction between endpoint evidence that establishes fulfillment and comparison evidence that only supports that judgment; do not require both checks when the endpoint is clear. The abbreviated binding (“The woman (...) helmet to the woman”) is less precise than the full target description, so ensure typed edits retain an explicit reference to the woman in the source image and the helmet-on-head criterion.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s semantic judgment is well supported: the edited image visibly adds a helmet to the woman, and the source comparison confirms it was absent before. No change to the pass criterion is indicated. For robustness, keep the binding explicit about the woman in the source image and the helmet being worn on her head; treat endpoint evidence and comparison evidence as distinct support, not mandatory conjunctive checks. Preserve unknown when the relevant visual evidence is genuinely insufficient, rather than interpreting uncertainty as failure."}
